name: The Division of Nature (the fourfold classification of being)
plain_explanation: In his major work, On the Division of Nature, John the Scot divides all of 'Nature' -- which for him includes both what is and what is not -- into four classes: (1) what creates and is not created (God as Creator); (2) what creates and is created (the Platonic ideas, which subsist eternally in God); (3) what is created but does not create (particular things in space and time); and (4) what neither creates nor is created (God again, but now as the End and Purpose toward which all things return).
precise_definition: A fourfold ontological schema in which the first and fourth classes are both identified with God (as origin and as end respectively), the second class is the world of eternal Platonic ideas or prime causes constituting the Logos, and the third class is the world of particular, materially embodied things.
why_it_mattered: It structures John's entire pantheistic metaphysics: because everything that emanates from God strives to return to Him, the end of all things is identical with their beginning, making God simultaneously the Alpha and Omega of the created order -- a scheme with clear (if partly concealed) roots in Neoplatonic emanation and return.
historical_origin: Derived, according to Russell, indirectly from Aristotle's threefold distinction of moving-not-moved, moving-and-moved, and moved-but-not-moving (for the first three classes) and from Dionysius's doctrine that all things return into God (for the fourth).
examples: God as uncreated Creator (class 1) and as uncreated, non-creating End (class 4)
The Platonic ideas as the eternal yet created prime causes (class 2)
Physical things in space and time (class 3)
objections: Russell notes this pantheism, which refuses substantial reality to creatures, is contrary to Christian doctrine
influence_on_later_thinkers: Repeatedly condemned as heretical in the following centuries; Pope Honorius III ordered all copies burned in 1225, though the order was not efficiently carried out.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Directly implicates orthodox Christian doctrines of creation and the Trinity.
